Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Comes With a Virtual Color Reel to Help US Forget About the Appalling ID.4
20 photos
Photo: AutoYa Interior / YouTube
When the Volkswagen Group introduced the dedicated MEB architecture for electric vehicles, it also established a completely new series of models featuring a common ID. name derivative along with numbers for the namesake Volkswagen brand.
So, we have seen the Volkswagen ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, ID.6, ID.7, or ID.7 Tourer, and so on. The main split faction was the ID. Buzz, which is also spelled differently because there’s a space between ID. and the rest of the name. That’s confusing, right?
Well, we could have gotten accustomed to the confusion if the EVs were better. Luckily, Volkswagen has continuously strived to improve them, and now there’s a new generation of vehicles plus facelifts, like the Volkswagen ID.3 Neo, the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI plus ID. Cross, a barrage of models for China, as well as the very important all-new VW ID. Tiguan.
The latter was just revealed as the eagerly awaited Volkswagen ID.4 replacement, a more traditional SUV in terms of design and also featuring an interior brimming with physical controls, just like VW promised. The Volkswagen ID.4 is now retiring, and the ID. Tiguan will replace it along with the ID.5, coming to Europe first but also to the United States ‘at a later date.’
The gasoline, diesel, and hybrid VW Tiguan will continue to exist, and the ID. Tiguan will simply become its EV sibling, with a muscular look and sharp body lines. There are even classic door handles, thank goodness, along with interior physical controls for main functions – AC, the steering wheel, and more. There will be screens, too: a 10-inch digital instrument cluster, a central 15-inch infotainment screen, and also an optional 12-inch passenger screen.
There’s vehicle-to-load functionality, a 1.1 cu. ft. (32-liter) frunk, plus three powertrains: 58 kWh battery with 188 hp and RWD, plus the larger 77-kWh pack with 281 hp and RWD or 295 hp and AWD. What we didn’t get were additional exterior and interior colors: only a black or white option inside and a silver or yellow shade on the outside.
No worries, though, as the good folks over at the "AutoYa" info channel on YouTube have a satellite venue dubbed " AutoYa Interior ," which is where all the CGI VW action resides, and they have a solution. The host of the channel doesn’t need to talk much, as they discuss a model that’s already official. Instead, he gives more time to the resident pixel master to show us the quick comparison to the older VW ID.4.
Afterward, they jump straight into the unofficial, hypothetical color reel, previewing the new model in various color options, like blue, red, green, brown, black, gray, or purple, both inside and outside – as a way to alleviate the fact that an official vehicle configurator tool isn’t available yet. So, what do you think? Do you have a favorite hue already?
